page: Microsoft Azure DC24s_v3 is a member of the DCSv3 server family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results place the DC24s_v3 in the average performance tier for most standard compute tasks. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is 1897.99, while the multi-core score reaches 45527.64. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 2531.67 GB/sec, dropping to 164.61 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write speed of 64.58 GB/sec. The server demonstrates strong performance in specific workloads, such as static web serving throughput at 42.52 GB/sec and Geekbench image processing at 15333.0.

For machine learning workloads, the server shows strong performance in small-scale LLM inference, achieving 2359.87 tokens/sec for prompt processing with a 135M model. However, performance drops significantly on larger models, with 70B model text generation falling into the bottom 25% tier at 2.74 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of local storage, this configuration is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and static web serving where external premium storage is utilized.
